subject: Version error: MI model with predictors of latent won't converge in new versions of lavaan and semTools

messages.author: 6403ad2aa9ae6d03
messages.subject: Version error: MI model with predictors of latent won't converge in new versions of lavaan and semTools
parts:
Hello,

I am running an MI model in which a latent variable is predicted by observed variables. I was able to get my model to run in old versions of lavaan (v. 06-5) and semTools (v. 0.5-2). However, since updating of lavaan (v. 06-7) and semTools (v. 0.5-3), the model converges, but the standard errors for the estimated parameters are not computed (i.e., they're returned as NA). 

My solution has been to simply re-install the old versions of the packages to run this code, which is fine. But I'm curious why this error occurs, and thought I ought to share this here. 

Here is my code:

### Baseline model

impEmpTheory <- '
factoremp =~ sympatheticNew + compassionate + moved + softhearted + warm + tender
'

# Regressions must be specified separately, because measEq.syntax() can't read syntax for structural regressions
impEmpRegressions <- '
## Regressions to control for manipulations

# Empathy instructions
factoremp ~ DemandCond + EmpathyCond + susp
'

### Estimate unidimensioanl configural invariant model

# Fit the model
impEmpConfigTheory <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = impEmpTheory, 
                              data = imp.dat.emp, 
                              ordered = c(
                                "sympatheticNew",
                                "compassionate", 
                                "moved", 
                                "softhearted", 
                                "warm", 
                                "tender"), 
                              parameterization = "delta", 
                              ID.fac = "std.lv", 
                              ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016", 
                              group = "SexCode", 
                              group.equal = "configural")

# Append the common factor model to the structural regressions 
impEmpConfiguralTheory <- c(as.character(impEmpConfigTheory), 
                            impEmpRegressions)

# Model fit
impEmpConfiguralTheoryFit <- cfa(as.character(impEmpConfiguralTheory),
                       data = imp.dat.emp,
                       group = "SexCode",
                       group.label = c("Male", "Female"),
                       ordered = c(
                         "sympatheticNew",
                         "compassionate", 
                         "moved", 
                         "softhearted", 
                         "warm", 
                         "tender"), 
                       test = "Satorra-Bentler")

# Summary
summary(impEmpConfiguralTheoryFit, 
        fit.measures = TRUE)

Thomas

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Version error: MI model with predictors of latent won't converge in new versions of lavaan and semTools
parts: I'm curious why this error occurs

Thanks for the syntax, although I can't do much with in without data.  However, I notice you have ordinal outcomes and exogenous covariates.  In this case, lavaan's default is fixed.x=TRUE and conditional.x=TRUE.  I used to override these both as FALSE in an earlier version of semTools (I forget whether it still happened in 0.5-2) because it took some extra programming to finally allow for those to be TRUE now.  You can try setting them FALSE in the new version to see whether the model runs like it used to, which would be interesting because convergence is usually easier when they are TRUE because fewer parameters need to be estimated.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 6403ad2aa9ae6d03
messages.subject: Re: Version error: MI model with predictors of latent won't converge in new versions of lavaan and semTools
parts:
Thanks, Terrence! Including the fixed.x=TRUE and conditional.x=TRUE commands did work: The model converged, and the results are qualitatively identical to those obtained when running with 0.5-2. 

However, I did get three warning messages:

Warning messages:
1: In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], wt = WT[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix
2: In muthen1984(Data = X[[g]], wt = WT[[g]], ov.names = ov.names[[g]],  :
  lavaan WARNING: trouble constructing W matrix; used generalized inverse for A11 submatrix
3: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)
    does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue
    (= -2.743280e-18) is smaller than zero. This may be a symptom that
    the model is not identified.

I don't read too much into these errors, but thought I ought to share them.

Also, the parameter estimates and fit indices are different than those estimated in 0.5-2, and the differences are greater than that which might be due to a rounding error. I suppose that is expected, since I am now estimating six new parameters for the covariances between exogenous predictors in both groups (although the degrees of freedom for the two models are identical).

I'd be happy to share my data or other code, if that's in any way helpful. Thanks again for your time and consideration.

Best,
Thomas

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Version error: MI model with predictors of latent won't converge in new versions of lavaan and semTools
parts: I did get three warning messages:

I expect they are all related.  The third indicates some linear dependency (multicollinearity) among estimated sampling distributions of estimated parameters (e.g., in samples where parameter A is lower, parameters B and C are higher, and the correlation is nearly perfect).  The negative eigenvalue is effectively zero, and might only appear negative due to machine error (R can't be precise to 18 decimals).  So unless there are other indications of lack of identification, I wouldn't worry too much.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
